age.evidence: Saline and psilocybin were administered on day 21 (PND 52)... animals were sacrificed on day 63 (PND 94). OPS was evaluated on days 51-55 (PND 82-86).

sex.evidence: Twenty-two female Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats... n = 8/group [4 groups]

dosing.evidence: A single bolus injection of sterile saline or psilocybin in saline vehicle (1 mg/kg) was administered IP at a volume of 1 mL/kg, 1 week after the final restraint session on day 21.

handling.evidence: Rats were solo housed with a standard 12:12 light-dark cycle, handled daily

enrichment_housing.evidence: cages included Bed-r'Nest enrichment (The Andersons, Inc., Maumee, OH)

assays.assay_description: 66 cm diameter circular arena; rats explore freely for 5 min (baseline) then 3 min test after 60-min ITI; one of two identical objects displaced by 6, 12, 18, 24 cm over five nightly sessions; discrimination index calculated from time exploring moved vs stationary objects.

application_type.evidence: psilocybin in saline vehicle (1 mg/kg) was administered IP

setup_habituation.evidence: For two consecutive nights (days 49-50) before the first OPS session, rats were habituated to the arena with the camera mounted overhead and both pairs of objects in random locations for 20 min

setup_restrain.evidence: allowing the rats to explore freely

food_restriction.evidence: No food was placed in the arena during the sessions; ad libitum access in the home cage.

water_restriction.evidence: No water was placed in the arena during the sessions.

time_to_assay.evidence: Saline and psilocybin were administered on day 21 (PND 52), OPS was evaluated on days 51-55 (PND 82-86)

outcomes.summary: A single dose of psilocybin given 30 days earlier rescued pattern separation in stressed rats: RP rats were able to discriminate at 24 cm displacement while RS rats could not discriminate at any displacement. NRS and NRP rats both discriminated at 24 cm.
outcomes.statistics: NRS: F(4,28)=4.622, p=0.0054, discriminated at 18 cm (p=0.0322) and 24 cm (p=0.0112); RS: F(4,28)=3.319, p=0.0119, no discrimination; NRP: discriminated at 12 cm (p=0.0398) and 24 cm (p=0.0025); RP: discriminated at 24 cm (p=0.0024).
outcomes.evidence: RP rats able to discriminate between moved and stationary objects at 24 cm (p = 0.0024)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Seconds spent exploring the moved object (T moved) and seconds spent exploring the stationary object (T stationary) were scored... discrimination index (DI) was calculated

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Each test was recorded as a single 3-min session; comparisons across nights are between-session, not within-session temporal dynamics.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences or transitions was reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Exploration was defined as the rat's nose being within 2 cm of the object and directed at the object

B5_social.evidence: Rats tested alone; no social component.

B6_cognitive.evidence: OPS assesses DG-CA3-specific cognitive function (pattern separation)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: scored by hand using Movie Maker video editing software

B8_multivariate.evidence: Only repeated measures ANOVA used; no multivariate analysis.

E1_environment_type.evidence: 66 cm diameter circular arena atop a plastic fold-out table

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter or refuge described in the arena.

E3_bedding.evidence: Arena atop a plastic fold-out table; no bedding mentioned.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in the testing arena.

E5_enrichment.evidence: Only test objects present; no enrichment objects.

E6_spatial.evidence: 66 cm diameter circular arena - single open compartment.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the arena.

D1_continuity.evidence: OPS sessions occurred once nightly for the following five nights

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowed the rats to explore freely for 5 min... recorded by an overhead camera for 3 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: OPS was evaluated on days 51-55 (5 nights)

D4_baseline.evidence: The first OPS session established a baseline by placing both identical objects in Pair A at the zero position (0/0)

D5_followup.evidence: Saline and psilocybin were administered on day 21... OPS was evaluated on days 51-55

assays.assay_description: 15-min pre-exposure swim on day before test, then 5-min test swim in a cylindrical tank (114 cm height x 30.5 cm diameter, 30 cm water, 28-30°C); immobility, swimming and climbing scored by trained observers blind to treatment using modified sampling.

application_type.evidence: psilocybin in saline vehicle (1 mg/kg) was administered IP

setup_habituation.evidence: a 15-min pre-exposure to the paradigm 1 day before testing is required to elicit consistent passive coping strategy

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were placed into a plastic cylindrical tank... that contained 30 cm of water... such that the rats could not support themselves by touching the bottom

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the tank during the swim.

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water accessible during the swim.

time_to_assay.evidence: Saline and psilocybin were administered on day 21... forced swim behavior was evaluated on day 57 or 58

outcomes.summary: A single dose of psilocybin given 36-37 days earlier reduced immobility and increased swimming in stressed (RP) rats to levels comparable to non-stressed controls. Psilocybin had no effect in non-stressed rats. Stress alone increased immobility and decreased swimming.
outcomes.statistics: Immobility: stress F(1,28)=22.99, p<0.0001; treatment F(1,28)=11.99, p=0.0017; interaction F(1,28)=16.68, p=0.0003. Swimming: interaction F(1,28)=4.656, p=0.0397; stress F(1,28)=8.936, p=0.0058; treatment F(1,28)=7.356, p=0.0113. Climbing: interaction F(1,28)=4.308, p=0.0472.
outcomes.evidence: RS rats were more immobile than NRS rats (p < 0.0001) and RP rats (p < 0.0001)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Immobility, swimming, and climbing were quantified (Fig. 4a-c).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total counts across the 5-min swim; no within-session time course reported.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences or transitions.

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility, swimming, and climbing are not natural ethological behaviours per rubric.

B6_cognitive.evidence: FST measures coping strategy, not learning/memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: FST scoring was performed by trained scorers blind to the treatment options

B8_multivariate.evidence: Two-way ANOVA only; no multivariate analysis.

E1_environment_type.evidence: plastic cylindrical tank (114 cm height · 30.5 cm diameter)

E2_shelter.evidence: No refuge in the FST tank.

E3_bedding.evidence: Tank contained water only; no bedding.

E7_social_context.evidence: Each rat tested alone; fresh water used for each animal.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or drinking water accessible during the swim.

D1_continuity.evidence: 15-min pre-exposure 1 day before testing; 5-min test swim

D2_session_duration.evidence: After a 15-min swim, the rats were removed

D3_recording_days.evidence: 15-min pre-exposure 1 day before testing; 5-min test on day 57 or 58

D4_baseline.evidence: Pre-exposure swim is a procedural priming step; the paper does not report data from it.

D5_followup.evidence: Psilocybin given day 21; FST on day 57/58 (>5 weeks post-dose)

assays.assay_description: Square open field arena (61 cm x 61 cm, walls 45 cm high); 5-min free exploration; distance traveled tracked using EthoVision XT 8.5; assessed immediately before each FST as a locomotor control.

application_type.evidence: psilocybin in saline vehicle (1 mg/kg) was administered IP

setup_habituation.evidence: No habituation to the open field arena is described.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowing the rats to explore freely for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the open field arena.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the open field arena.

time_to_assay.evidence: LCA was assessed immediately before each FST [day 57 or 58]; psilocybin given on day 21.

outcomes.summary: No differences in overall locomotor activity (distance traveled) were observed among groups, indicating that psilocybin and stress effects in the FST were not driven by nonspecific locomotor changes.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA: no significant effects of stress or treatment on distance traveled (Fig. 4d).
outcomes.evidence: No differences in overall LCA were observed among groups

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single total distance reported; no within-session bins.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: EthoVision XT 8.5 tracking software - position tracking, not behavioural classification.

E1_environment_type.evidence: square open field arena (61 cm 2) with opaque walls 45 cm high

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the arena.

D1_continuity.evidence: allowing the rats to explore freely for 5 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: LCA assessed immediately before each FST (one day per animal).

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug open field recording reported.

D5_followup.evidence: LCA assessed on day 57/58, >5 weeks after psilocybin dosing on day 21.

judge_notes: Three behavioural assays identified by all candidates: OPS, FST, and Open Field (locomotor control). All retained.
time_to_assay set to long_term_over7d for all assays (>30 days post-dose); some candidates incorrectly chose short_term_1to7d.

FST D2 scored 1 (15-60 min) because the 15-min pre-exposure swim is data-collected (FST behaviour cannot be 'recorded' without it being a recording session per study design); FST D4 scored 0 because no pre-exposure swim data is reported.
OPS B2 scored 0: comparison across nightly displacements is between-session, not within-session temporal dynamics per rubric.
OPS time_to_assay value_minutes set to first OPS day (day 51 - day 21 = 30 days = 43200 min).
